title: Salvation and the Church
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Salvation and the church teaches that those saved by Christ are joined to His people. Salvation is personal, but it does not leave believers isolated from the body of Christ.
summary: Salvation and the church teaches that those saved by Christ are joined to His people. Salvation is personal, but it does not leave believers isolated from the body of Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ saves a people for Himself and builds His church. Those united to Him are also brought into fellowship, worship, service, accountability, and mission with His body.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Salvation brings believers into relationship with God and with God’s people. The church is not an optional add-on to the Christian life, but the gathered people Christ purchased and is building.

Those saved by Christ become members of one body. Each believer needs the body, and the body needs each member. No Christian is designed for isolated self-rule.

The saved community devotes itself to teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread, prayer, worship, generosity, and witness. These are not merely programs; they are signs of shared life in Christ.

The church also becomes a place of care, correction, service, and mission. Saved people are formed together as a people who display Christ to the world.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people have been hurt by churches or have learned to live disconnected from the body. This doctrine does not deny wounds, but it reminds believers that Christ still saves people into a family.

It also challenges individualistic faith. Jesus did not save believers to be spiritual consumers, but members of His body who worship, serve, love, and grow together.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not treat salvation as a private possession disconnected from Christ’s people. Seek faithful fellowship, worship, accountability, service, and mutual encouragement. If you carry church hurt, bring it to Christ honestly while asking Him to lead you toward healthy, biblical community.
